content: Best practice for Senior Software Engineer JD: Clearly separate must-have skills (3-5 years experience, proficiency in core tech stack) from nice-to-have skills (additional frameworks, certifications). Use action-oriented language to describe responsibilities.

Effective JD structure: 1) Company overview (2-3 sentences), 2) Role summary (1 paragraph), 3) Key responsibilities (5-7 bullet points), 4) Required qualifications (must-have), 5) Preferred qualifications (nice-to-have), 6) Benefits and perks.

Avoid gender-biased language in job descriptions. Use neutral terms like 'they/their' instead of 'he/she'. Replace 'rockstar' or 'ninja' with 'skilled' or 'experienced'. This increases application rates by 30%.

For Product Manager roles: Emphasize cross-functional collaboration, data-driven decision making, and user-centric mindset. Include metrics ownership and stakeholder management in key responsibilities.
Salary transparency in JDs increases application quality by 40%. Include salary range or mention 'competitive salary based on experience' to set clear expectations.
For junior positions: Focus on learning opportunities, mentorship programs, and growth potential. De-emphasize years of experience and emphasize willingness to learn and foundational skills.
